name: Bootstrapping Domain Evals Without Public Benchmarks
claim_sentence: Public benchmarks never measure a team's real task, so builders must engineer bespoke evaluation loops—synthesizing inputs from known answers, replaying historical outages, backtesting dated web snapshots, and grading trajectories with behavior rubrics—or redesign the agent until it is evaluable.
definition: Across enterprise RAG, legal review, creative writing, code review, accounting, and quantitative investing, speakers converged on the same wall: off-the-shelf benchmarks tell you nothing about whether your agent works, and domain experts cannot hand-grade thousands of runs. Air Canada inverted dataset creation by generating questions from known source pages and populating legal templates with clauses engineered to breach or pass rules, even re-architecting an agent purely to make it deterministically evaluable. Greptile benchmarks prompt changes against historical outage-causing PRs; Bridgewater hand-labeled 200 investment queries in a week to lift precision@10 from 60% to 95%; Exa Snapshot backtests predictive agents against 400 billion dated web pages without lookahead leakage; Towards AI runs five drafts per prompt under a two-stage cross-family rubric; and Basis grades ground-truth-free production runs with behavior specs and trajectory forking. The sharp counter-position centers on the grader itself: Sonar and Air Canada both showed that uncalibrated LLM-as-judge verdicts flip across identical runs and add noise rivaling the agent's own error rate.

name: Token Economics, Right-Sizing, and Open Foundations
claim_sentence: As frontier intelligence commoditizes while aggregate token bills surge, durable economics come from attributing spend per workload, routing subtasks to fast specialist or open-weight models, tuning serving concurrency and KV caches, and owning a model-swappable stack rather than renting lock-in from frontier labs.
definition: Practitioners attacked runaway inference costs across every layer below default frontier API calls. Featherless showed that splitting API keys by department, reserving superlinear low-latency serving (3x cost per 2x speed) for interactive paths, and leveraging higher tokens-per-second to entice developers onto smaller worker models deliver immediate ROI. Runpod's BenchPod tunes vLLM nightly builds, batch-token concurrency, and 4xH200 DeepSeek deployments live without 30-minute cold starts; Greptile routes 20 review subtasks across small and frontier models; Exa cuts trajectory tokens 95% via dynamic snippet highlights; Towards AI merges ten cheap GLM/Flash drafts with one high-thinking pass; and Ramp pairs frontier orchestrators with post-trained 35B Qwen models, 5x-cheaper open-weight security swarms, and semantic spend taxonomies—even as Apify warned that heavily subsidized flat-rate plans distort build-versus-buy incentives. Strategically, Nous Research argued that shrinking token margins force frontier labs to seek lock-in at the enterprise agent layer and compete vertically, making open, model-agnostic foundations essential. The counter-arguments cut both ways: naive turn-by-turn multi-model routing destroys prefix KV-cache hit rates, while falling frontier unit prices tempt teams to scale on frontier platforms rather than maintain custom post-training.

name: Sandboxed Computers, Context Architecture, and the Shrinking Harness
claim_sentence: As frontier models absorb prompt-level coding tricks through a user-trajectory data flywheel, the durable agent harness converges on two layers models cannot internalize: isolated create-run-delete VM sandboxes and outer-loop context engines that supply institutional intent, living codebase maps, and precomputed KV caches.
definition: OpenHands framed the central paradox of 2026 harness design: coding scaffolding makes harder tasks tractable, user trajectories feed model post-training, and models absorb those habits until harness choice barely moves coding benchmark scores—motivating self-cleaning guardrail shims that watcher bots delete once newer models stop triggering them. What models cannot absorb defines the lasting architecture. First is the execution boundary: Daytona showed that every competing framework reduces to create-run-delete VM primitives and is actively deleting local executors because embedded runtimes still expose host tools and a single allowed `python -c` command compromises the host; Arize and Greptile isolate every run in disposable sandboxes while persisting memory externally. Second is outer-loop context: Linear showed that five-cent intelligence shifts failure from coding capacity to product incoherence unless triage agents assemble customer value, logs, and prior decisions upfront; Greptile replaces grep with a living company wiki; Sonar Vortex feeds structural maps in-loop to cut token spend 36%; Ramp compresses 20–30x month-end context into offline KV-cache cartridges; GEICO routes edge-case HTML worksheets to domain owners; and Basis treats every working-window token as runtime training data. Yet as OpenHands noted in counter-point, entering unmastered domains like autonomous multi-agent colleagues immediately forces teams to re-add heavy prompting, coordinator hierarchies, and guardrails.

name: Bounded Autonomy, Runtime Governance, and the Enterprise Diffusion Gap
claim_sentence: Outside software engineering, enterprise agents remain near 5% production adoption not for lack of raw model intelligence, but because non-deterministic workers require institutional trust infrastructure—automatic registries, build-time policy DAGs, risk-tiered entitlements, and opinionated workflows—between reckless autonomy and paralyzing lockdown.
definition: Tenex quantified the conference's starkest macro reality: across roughly 100 large enterprises, general-purpose LLM access sits near 90% and coding agents near 50%, yet autonomous agents in non-engineering business workflows sit around 5%. Anthropic, Apollo, GEICO, Basis, and Apify all traced that diffusion gap to governance, process, and trust friction rather than model IQ—with Apify showing that even after eighteen months of agent payment standards, 30-day volume sits near $1M on x402 and $1,500 on MPP because static API keys, untrusted endpoints requiring marketplace middlemen, and deferred-settlement double-spend risks dominate the funnel. The architectural remedy across regulated firms was bounded autonomy: Two Sigma replaces months-long manual review queues and rubber-stamp approval fatigue with automatic framework registration, risk-scored scrutiny, registry-compiled runtime entitlements, and conservative classifiers that escalate only ambiguous calls; Coinbase separates build-time normative policy ('the original institutional system prompt') from mutating runtime state inside compliance DAGs; Basis encodes opinionated, auditable tax and accounting workflows rather than 'Move 37' creativity; and Anthropic scopes financial agents with least-privilege identities and deterministic hooks gated on advisor or SME sign-off. Qualifying this optimism, Daytona showed that host-level policy allowlists collapse if an interpreter command is permitted, while GEICO's one-day war rooms proved outer-loop enterprise inertia can be broken when decision-makers sit inside the loop.

name: Deterministic Verification Loops Over Line-by-Line Review
claim_sentence: Because coding agents generate pull requests far faster than humans can read them—and reviewers accept wrong AI output four times out of five—shipping confidence must come from independent, multi-layered verification harnesses and runnable behavioral proofs rather than manual line-by-line diff inspection.
definition: Software delivery talks confronted the review bottleneck head-on: Sonar reported a 2,450% explosion in AI-generated code yielding only 30% more releases because human reviewers succumb to 'cognitive surrender' (agreeing with wrong AI output 80% of the time) while multi-step agent accuracy decays exponentially across long horizons. Teams moving toward lights-on and dark software factories replaced manual line reading with executable proof loops. In the verification workshop, external MCP gates (`Ctx`) refuse agent self-reports until deterministic CLI and Playwright checks verify backend persistence, making verifier suites more durable than the application code itself. At Anthropic, merging 30,000 daily changes relies on automated first-pass reviews, edit hooks, and browser-driven screenshot and video evidence; Sonar pairs CPU static analysis with GPU generative checks and CVE scanning across every loop; Greptile inverts author and reviewer model families (+10% bug catch) and boots full-stack VM sandboxes for vision-model UI QA; Linear wires verification skills and product-history review agents into unattended bug fixes; GEICO enforces deterministic nine-step artifact gates; Untangle caps builder-reviewer loops at three iterations; and Coinbase runs parallel agent reviews inside gated DAGs. Against pure automation, Untangle insisted that a human product owner watching each feature video remains irreducible, and Featherless warned that unowned generation lobs 'slop grenades' onto peers.

name: Self-Improving Fleets and the Agent Manager
claim_sentence: Software engineering is shifting from writing code locally to managing asynchronous cloud agent fleets and closing the trace-to-skill loop—centralizing transcripts and tool calls, grading runs post-merge, and letting meta-agents distill recurring failures and human corrections into versioned skills.
definition: Across Warp, Arize, Linear, Untangle, GEICO, Anthropic, and Runpod, the unit of engineering work moved from crafting individual features to operating and improving the agent factory itself. Warp demonstrated 'factory engineering': shared cloud Docker sandboxes automatically centralize conversation transcripts, MCP/tool calls, and diffs, exposing silent agent workarounds (like brute-force port probing) to post-merge markdown judge rubrics and daily meta-agents (`Skill Doctor`) that open measurable skill PRs. Linear runs a daily post-merge distillation job that turns PR review corrections and reverts into `agents.md` updates; Arize designs agent-first telemetry to wake scheduled sandbox sweeps while tracing both production agents and the coding harnesses behind them; Anthropic treats SME-authored plain-text skills as living, versioned code co-iterated by business teams and engineers; GEICO coordinates legacy transformations through Markdown FleetKit protocols; Runpod exposes GPU benchmark controls as FastAPI endpoints for agents to drive directly; and Untangle replaces local development with communicating builder, reviewer, and merge-manager sessions—extending the paradigm to hiring by stack-ranking candidates on 45-minute recorded agent-operating trials, echoing the Day 2 keynote's call to pair human company curation with career-research agents. In tension with universal 'agent management,' Basis warned that pushing prompt and skill authorship onto non-technical enterprise users creates a severe competency gap, and Day 2's keynote cautioned against letting agents automate personal outreach like resume submissions.
also_called: your job is now agent manager

name: Governed Ontologies, Provenance, and Financial Workbenches
claim_sentence: In institutional investing and private markets, off-the-shelf web chatbots fail on stale or conflicting inputs; agents earn front-office trust only atop governed firm ontologies, validated golden sources, unified MCP connectors, and hybrid code-ML-LLM-human pipelines that write synthesis back into the vault.
definition: Every institutional finance talk located competitive advantage in governed data infrastructure and workflow design rather than raw model selection. Bridgewater contrasted an open-web chatbot answering a Korean won query from a single three-month-old note with Vault—which aligns 100M+ documents to a bitemporal ontology, serves 1,000+ QPS agent storms via turbopuffer cluster-local native filtering, migrates researcher email habits into saved collections, and writes human-agent workbench synthesis back into the corpus so knowledge compounds. At Apollo's Redding Ridge credit platform, engineers sat daily with portfolio managers to codify golden-source precedence across 20 conflicting systems, turning multi-hour weekly loan reconciliations into one-minute automated QA reports and cutting 200–400-name CLO portfolio construction from days in Excel to minutes for the first 80–90%. Coatue modeled the hedge fund as a composite state-machine function `(external_context, internal_context) -> (stock, size, timing)`, insisting that every pixel a human sees must be API-accessible while assigning each step whichever runner—deterministic code, classical ML, LLM, or human—maximizes quality. Exa supplied the external temporal layer with 400 billion dated web snapshots built for dense exploratory agent queries, while Anthropic standardized multi-system enterprise access behind a single MCP connectivity layer.
why_uncontested: No speaker argued that general-purpose models or ungrounded web search could support institutional capital allocation without proprietary governed data; Apollo, Bridgewater, and Coatue unanimously restricted ungrounded chat to low-stakes background research.

name: Spatiotemporal World Models and Real-Time Simulation
claim_sentence: Scaling laws extend beyond turn-based text to continuous video and action streams, turning pixels-to-actions policies and next-frame predictors into real-time world simulators that internalize physics, control robots, and replace static 3D engines with interactive visual interfaces.
definition: General Intuition and Runway pushed AI engineering past autoregressive text into continuous space and time. General Intuition argued that real-time agents must observe while acting, leveraging Medal's gameplay pipeline—scaling toward three billion videos a year and 1.5 trillion monthly controller actions—because high-APM game controllers share the exact action space of low-DOF robot teleoperation and plug neatly as reactive control layers beneath frontier LLM planners. Runway bet on compute scaling laws for next-frame video prediction, demonstrating that models trained at scale internalize geometry, gravity, occlusion, and object permanence directly from pixels—unlocking action-conditioned robotics simulators, engine-free World Interface Models with no Unity or Blender mesh underneath, interactive Continuum video portals, and visual scratchpads where coding agents simulate spatial designs alongside code. Their sharpest technical disagreement sits on supervision: General Intuition contended that explicit controller action labels transfer far better to real-time control than passive video-only latent inference because subtle inputs like aircraft rudder adjustments leave almost no trace in raw pixel frames.
